subject: Private deployment feasibility call - hyperscaler gap analysis & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: infra-eval@hyperscaler.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Private deployment feasibility call - next validation items

Alex / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the validation items we agreed would be helpful to prioritize: 

1) Network topology and egress: confirmation of which IP ranges and ports your control plane would need to reach from our VPC / air-gapped site. We need explicit source/destination CIDRs and whether STS endpoints (TLS) are required.

2) Control-plane reachability modes: you mentioned a managed control plane and a tunnel-based connector. Please confirm whether an "offline control plane" / broker model is supported for fully isolated sites.

3) Installer & air-gap options: we need a concise installer flow that our infra team can run in an air-gapped environment (tarball/OCI images, install steps, expected run time, and any dependency network calls).

4) KMS/HSM integration: customer requires support for external KMS and HSM-backed keys for key material — docs or examples appreciated.

5) Performance baseline: target network/throughput tests (p99 latency goals, tokens/sec at 8k context) and a suggested workload for apples-to-apples comparison vs the hyperscaler API.

6) Failure modes & fallback: what happens if the control-plane link is interrupted — local inference only? automatic fallback to a lighter model?

I've attached a short connectivity checklist and a sample network trace template that our infra team will populate. Please reply with links to your runbook and any clarifying notes.

Goal: turn this into a short test plan we can run next week (target window: Nov 23–25) and a clear gap map of where your offering differs from Redwood's private deployment model.

Thanks,
Jordan
Principal AE, Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-private-connectivity-checklist.pdf]
From: Alex Rivera <infra-eval@hyperscaler.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment feasibility call - next validation items

Jordan — appreciate the structured ask, this is very helpful. Quick responses inline and a few links.

On Wed, 18 Nov 2026 at 14:12, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Network topology and egress: confirmation of which IP ranges and ports your control plane would need to reach from our VPC / air-gapped site.

We can provide a CIDR list for the regions you pick (US-Central / US-West). Control-plane uses TLS over 443 for management and a TCP range 15000-15100 for telemetry streams. We will prepare a minimal IP list (will attach as a runbook snippet).

> 2) Control-plane reachability modes: you mentioned a managed control plane and a tunnel-based connector. Please confirm whether an "offline control plane" / broker model is supported for fully isolated sites.

Short answer: we do not currently have a fully offline broker model. Our connector supports outbound-only tunnels to our managed control plane; intermittent connectivity is tolerated but some control-plane features (rollouts, metrics) will be delayed.

> 3) Installer & air-gap options: we need a concise installer flow that our infra team can run in an air-gapped environment (tarball/OCI images, install steps, expected run time, and any dependency network calls).

We have an on-prem bundle (OCI tarball + installer) but it requires an initial bootstrap to validate licensing over the Internet. Full offline install is on our roadmap; we can detail workarounds (manual license injection).

> 4) KMS/HSM integration: customer requires support for external KMS and HSM-backed keys for key material — docs or examples appreciated.

We support KMS integrations (cloud vendor KMS) and have an HSM connector for premium customers. Will share integration guide.

> 5) Performance baseline: target network/throughput tests (p99 latency goals, tokens/sec at 8k context) and a suggested workload for apples-to-apples comparison vs the hyperscaler API.

We can provide a benchmark harness and sample traces. Note that our pricing/throughput assumptions differ significantly in sustained token workloads vs short-burst API calls.

> 6) Failure modes & fallback: what happens if the control-plane link is interrupted — local inference only? automatic fallback to a lighter model?

If the connector drops, running instances continue serving cached models, but new deployment/config changes won't land. No automatic model downgrade currently; that requires a pre-configured fallback policy.

I'll attach the runbook snippets and IP list in a follow-up. Happy to jump on a quick 30m with your infra/security leads if helpful.

— Alex
Infrastructure Evals, Hyperscaler Cloud

[attachment: hyperscaler-runbook-link.txt]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment feasibility call - next validation items

Looping in our Security/Platform quick notes: 
- We should validate that the connector's outbound tunnel can be pinned to specific IP ranges and does not require DNS-based allowlists.
- For the HSM ask: ask for STS flow and key rotation doc; customer will insist on non-exportable keys.
- Recommend we schedule the bandwidth/throughput test (tokens/sec) during off-hours and capture p50/p95/p99.

I can draft the specific test commands for the infra team once Alex shares the runbook. Stephanie — can you lead the scheduling with FinSecure?

Naomi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, infra-eval@hyperscaler.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment feasibility call - next validation items

Thanks all — action list and owners below. Please treat this as our working test plan and update the attached checklist accordingly.

Action items (owners):
- Alex / Hyperscaler: share minimal IP/port list + runbook snippets (deadline: 11/23 EOD). [external]
- Stephanie: schedule bandwidth + latency validation window with FinSecure for 11/24 00:00–04:00 PST and confirm infra contacts (deadline: 11/23). [internal]
- Naomi: draft HSM/KMS verification checklist and key rotation questions for the security PO. (deadline: 11/24). [internal]
- Jordan & Product: prepare an apples-to-apples benchmark harness (tokens/sec with 8k context) and one short prompt test to surface quality differences; baseline run target 11/24. (deadline: 11/25).

Competitive notes for the readout (for internal use):
- Hyperscaler gap: no fully offline control-plane/broker option today; reliance on outbound tunnel and intermittent connectivity model.
- Differentiators to highlight for Redwood: explicit offline-install path, optional private control-plane (customer-managed), deterministic per-token economics with batching/kv cache, built-in canary/fallback policies.
- Risk: Hyperscaler's initial installer requires an online bootstrap for licensing; this is likely a blocker for strict air-gapped customers unless manual licensing is accepted.

Attachments: redwood-private-connectivity-checklist.pdf, network-trace-template.txt, hyperscaler-runbook-link.txt

Next sync: 11/25 10:00 PST to review filled connectivity checklist and the first benchmark results. HubSpot: HubSpot_12345.

-Jordan
Principal AE, Redwood Inference
